description: The bar chart, titled "% point difference" and associated with the paper "Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models," compares the performance differences between two models—mBERT (light blue) and XLM-R (dark blue)—across four distinct experimental conditions. The horizontal axis displays these conditions, labeled as "hidden:[50], linear," "hidden:[], linear," "hidden:[100], ReLU," and "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU," which likely represent different model configurations or layers. The vertical axis, labeled "% point difference," ranges from -0.2 to 0.2, indicating the percentage point difference in performance, with zero as the baseline. The legend in the top right corner identifies the light blue bars as mBERT and the dark blue bars as XLM-R. The chart shows that for the first condition ("hidden:[50], linear"), both models have negative differences, with mBERT at approximately -0.18 and XLM-R at about -0.08. In the second condition ("hidden:[], linear"), mBERT shows a positive difference of approximately 0.06, while XLM-R shows a much larger positive difference of about 0.20. For the third condition ("hidden:[100], ReLU"), mBERT has a negative difference of around -0.09, and XLM-R has a small positive difference of about 0.03. In the final condition ("hidden:[50, 50], ReLU"), both models have negative differences, with mBERT at approximately -0.15 and XLM-R at about -0.11. The data suggests that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT in the second and third conditions, while mBERT performs better in the first and fourth conditions.
